subject.title: [Bug]: CLI relay exits silently with code 1 when session lane is blocked — no timeout or busy error surfaced

question: Should the CLI convert a same-session lane wait into a terminal busy result, and what exit/error contract should scripts rely on?
rationale: The code fix is narrow, but the candidate behavior changes user-visible delivery semantics and exit handling for queued CLI dispatches.

options.title: Adopt terminal CLI busy result
options.body: Have Gateway return structured lane-wait details to CLI text/JSON callers after the threshold while leaving non-CLI callers queued.

options.title: Only improve timeout messaging
options.body: Keep queued execution semantics and surface a clearer generic timeout/failure message without rejecting queued work early.

options.title: Defer contract until broader queue policy
options.body: Pause the linked PR and settle CLI queueing semantics separately before changing the relay behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt terminal CLI busy result
recommendation.body: Have Gateway return structured lane-wait details to CLI text/JSON callers after the threshold while leaving non-CLI callers queued.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger is the strongest available routing candidate for the CLI/Gateway behavior contract from current and diagnostic-path history.
